item.title: Easing H0 tension with Constrained Cosmological Parameters in f(R,Lm) Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We constrain two f(R,Lm) gravity models formulated through power-law and exponential curvature--matter couplings to evaluate their late-time dynamics and capacity to alleviate the H0 tension. Using MCMC sampling within the Cobaya framework, we confront both models against Cosmic Chronometer, Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae, and DESI-DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data under uniform and local SH0ES Gaussian H0 priors, benchmarking performance against flat Lambda_CDM via Delta_AIC, Delta_BIC, and Delta_DIC. In the unanchored joint analysis, both extensions are statistically favored over Lambda_ CDM (Delta_BIC = -6.60 and -2.91, respectively) and drive a smooth transition to late-time acceleration at z_t between 0.62-0.67 for the power-law model and z_t between 0.56-0.60 for the exponential model. Relative to the unanchored LambdaCDM constraint of H0 = 68.24 \pm 0.39\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}} which is around $4.3\sigma$ tension with SH0ES, the power-law model yields $H0 = 67.00 \pm 1.04\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ ($4.1\sigma$), whereas the exponential model modestly elevates H0 to $69.46 \pm 0.70\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, easing the tension to $2.9\sigma$ without local calibration. Under the SH0ES prior, the power-law model exhibits dataset-dependent phantom excursions $q \to -1.21$, $\omega_{\mathrm{eff}} \to -1.14$ in $CC+H0$ and incurs a strong Bayesian penalty in the full joint fit Delta_BIC = +7.42. Conversely, the exponential model maintains strict quintessence-like stability, converging smoothly to the de Sitter attractor ($q \to -1$, $\omega_{\mathrm{eff}} \to -1$) while reducing the SH0ES discrepancy to $1.8\sigma$ ($H0 = 70.60 \pm 0.86\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$) with positive Akaike support (Delta_AIC = -4.29) and only a mild Bayesian complexity penalty (Delta_BIC = +1.17).
item.dc:creator: Y. Kalpana Devi, B. Mishra, Francisco Tello-Ortiz

item.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures of Compact Extra Dimensions and Their Detectability with Third-Generation Interferometers
item.description: arXiv:2611.31279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate gravitational-wave dynamics in theories of gravity formulated in $D=4+N$ dimensions, with matter localized on a four-dimensional brane or coupled to the effective four-dimensional metric obtained after compactification. We consider four representative geometries, namely toroidal and Calabi--Yau compactifications, and the warped Randall--Sundrum I and II models, which cover the principal discrete and continuous Kaluza--Klein spectra. We derive the modifications of binary dynamics, propagation, quasinormal modes and polarization content, and use them as a feasibility screening for third-generation interferometers, with particular attention to the Einstein Telescope. The screening shows that the direct effects of the heavy Kaluza--Klein towers are strongly suppressed and are expected to be inaccessible to third-generation detectors. Indeed, the effective-field-theory corrections scale as $(\hbar\omega/m_1c^2)^2$$\sim$$10^{-23}$--$10^{-22}$, while the explicit conservative inspiral-phase correction of RS2 remains below the ET measurability threshold over the region allowed by laboratory bounds. Nevertheless, the screening identifies additional phenomenological channels that may remain testable: a tidal-charge deformation of the black-hole background, which shifts the QNM frequencies and damping times; a continuum-inspired phase deformation; and a radion-induced scalar polarization. We treat these channels as phenomenological benchmarks and formulate a Fisher-matrix Monte Carlo forecast based on the Earth-fixed geometry of the candidate sites, comparing the triangular and double-L Einstein Telescope configurations within an idealized common-noise setting.
item.dc:creator: M. D. C. Torri

item.title: Strong-lensing tests of angular structure in the radial acceleration relation
item.description: arXiv:2611.31281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The radial acceleration relation (RAR) links the radial acceleration inferred from galaxy rotation curves to that predicted from the observed baryonic distribution. Whether it has a counterpart in the angular structure of gravitational fields remains unknown. We develop an observational framework to test for such a non radial correspondence using strong gravitational lenses, without assuming that a generalized RAR exists. The singular perturbative approach reconstructs two angular fields from lensed image morphology without imposing a parametric mass profile. We separate contributions from projected mass inside and outside the Einstein circle, normalize the inner baryonic and total fields, and define statistical comparisons of their radial and tangential components. We also derive higher order potential multipoles for a smooth elliptical, off centered projected halo and evaluate their dependence on NFW and Einasto profiles. The inner outer separation isolates the projected internal contribution most directly relevant to the RAR comparison. The inner dipole coefficients can be recovered without the source position contribution when both reconstructed fields are used. The quadrupole phase provides a measure of projected orientation, while the higher order moments quantify departures from a smooth elliptical profile. For the profiles and parameter ranges considered, the predicted higher order ratios remain small and vary only moderately with the Einstein radius to scale radius ratio. The framework provides a model independent observational test of whether a three dimensional non radial baryonic Total field correspondence leaves a statistical imprint after projection. The large strong lens population expected from Euclid could provide the sample needed for this test, subject to image quality, photometric, and selection function requirements.
item.dc:creator: C. Alard

item.title: CPL dark energy: exact pressure-density relation and limits on cosmic acceleration
item.description: arXiv:2611.31283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parametrization, $w=w_0+w_a(1-a)$, is widely used to assess current indications of evolving dark energy. We ask what the parametrization itself imposes, independently of the data. First, we invert its pressure-density relation in closed form using the real branches of the Lambert $W$ function, and classify its positive-density histories with $w_a\ne0$ into six classes. Every history that crosses $w=-1$ reduces, in normalized variables, to one parameter-free curve, folded at a density extremum: the equation of state has two parameters, and the third only locates the present on the curve. No single-valued barotropic fluid follows the curve through the fold, so a crossing requires a continuation prescription. Second, we prove that a separately conserved, positive-density component accompanied by dust, radiation and collisionless massive species produces at most one accelerating epoch on a connected expanding branch, for any spatial curvature, if $w$ is nondecreasing and convex in $\ln a$, or nonincreasing; counterexamples delimit these hypotheses. For CPL with $w_a<0$, the case relevant to the DESI mean values, we give the exact dust-limit condition for an accelerating window to exist and an accurate approximation to its edges. At the DESI DR2 mean values the window is still open today for the three combinations that include supernovae, and closed at $z\simeq0.07$ for BAO+CMB alone. Conditional on $w_a<0$ and continued CPL evolution, any accelerating window is bounded; observations constrain its existence and location.
item.dc:creator: \"Ozg\"ur Akarsu, Maria Caruana, Luis A. Escamilla, Emre O. Kahya

item.title: Reheating Constraints on the $\alpha$-Starobinsky Model and Implications for Inflation Decays
item.description: arXiv:2611.31285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We constrain the $\alpha$-Starobinsky model of inflation with an explicit reheating sector, in which the number of $e$-folds $N_*$ is computed for every sampled point from the reheating equation of state $w_{\mathrm{rh}}$ and temperature $T_{\mathrm{rh}}$, using a fully numerical pivot-scale matching in $\mathtt{CLASS}$. We analyze six combinations of Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. The CMB sees reheating only through $\ln R_{\rm rad}\simeq N_*-N_{\rm inst}$, the shift of $N_*$ from its instantaneous-reheating value. At $\alpha=1$, Planck gives $n_s=0.9656^{+0.0015}_{-0.0017}$ and is consistent with instantaneous reheating, $\ln R_{\rm rad}=0.4\pm2.7$. Planck, ACT and DESI together (P-ACT+DESI) give $n_s=0.9689^{+0.0012}_{-0.0016}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6.5^{+2.5}_{-3.1}$, which prefers a stiff phase ($w_{\mathrm{rh}}>0.47$ at 95$\%$). With $\alpha$ free they give $\log_{10}\alpha=1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.8}$, $n_s=0.9706^{+0.0016}_{-0.0020}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6^{+3}_{-4}$. This preference is not in agreement with the bound on the primordial gravitational-wave contribution. Imposing that bound approximately removes about half of the preferred stiff region. Comparing to an otherwise identical analysis in which $N_*$ is a free parameter, we find that the reheating sector acts mainly as a prior on $N_*$: at $\alpha=1$ it narrows the inflationary posteriors, and with $\alpha$ free it removes the largest values of $N_*$ and doubles the preferred $r$ for P-ACT+DESI. Finally, we briefly discuss the connection between these phenomenological constraints and representative perturbative inflaton decay scenarios, highlighting the limitations of this interpretation for stiff reheating histories.
item.dc:creator: Karim Carrion, Luis E. Padilla, Gabriel Germ\'an, Juan Carlos Hidalgo

item.title: Constraints on Finsler cosmology from observational data
item.description: arXiv:2611.31287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate current constraints and conditional detectability of Finslerian {\Lambda}CDM (F{\Lambda}CDM) cosmology using supernova, cosmic chronometer (CC), and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. We adopt PantheonPlus SH0ES, CC and BAO data with a free acoustic scale. Supplementary tests with DES supernovae and PantheonPlus without SH0ES absolute calibra?tion verify result robustness. We compare F{\Lambda}CDM model against {\Lambda}CDM and wCDM and find that F{\Lambda}CDM improves the fit compared to {\Lambda}CDM, but the degree of fit is not superior to that of the wCDM model with the same number of parameters. We find that the background variations introduced by F{\Lambda}CDM can be absorbed to some extent by {\Lambda}CDM through adjusting its own parameters. We then use parametric bootstrap calibration and Monte Carlo power estimation to assess the detection power of residual background deviation that {\Lambda}CDM cannot absorb. We find no statistically significant ev?idence for a residual background deviation in the main data configuration. For an injection background fixed at the maximum likelihood estimate, the conditional detection power is relatively low. We examine the sensitivity of the detection power of this signal to the injected background. We find that the detection power of this deviation is significantly dependent on the injection context.
item.dc:creator: Bohao Wang, Xiaofeng Yang, Kang Jiao, Yunliang Ren, Yangjun Shi, Jianfeng Meng, Jingze Li, Xiongwei Liu

item.title: The $\gamma = 1/2$ Problem: A Unified Viability Criterion for f(R) Gravity in the Solar System
item.description: arXiv:2611.31288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A novel framework for addressing both the accelerated expansion of the cosmos and the inflationary epoch involves modifying the Einstein-Hilbert action through a function $f(R)$. While these $f(R)$ gravity theories can, under certain conditions, replicate phenomena described by scalar-tensor theories, this is only viable if the associated scalar field can operate within the Solar System without violating stringent observational constraints. A significant challenge is that within this theoretical equivalence, the post-Newtonian parameter $\gamma$ is fixed at $\gamma = 1/2$, a value that deviates substantially from the experimentally established result of $\gamma \approx 1$. Recent discussions have questioned the genuine equivalence between $f(R)$ gravity and scalar-tensor formulations. Furthermore, recent findings, independent of this equivalence, have demonstrated that the field equations for $1/R$ theory predict $\gamma = 1/2$ in a vacuum for spherical mass distributions. In this work, we extend these results to a broader class of $f(R)$ functions, aiming to delineate the specific conditions that lead to the prediction of $\gamma = 1/2$. This investigation provides a unified framework for identifying which classes of $f(R)$ gravity can satisfy Solar System constraints, deriving a general viability criterion that moves beyond previous case-by-case analyses. We derive a unified viability criterion that provides a necessary condition for any $f(R)$ theory to satisfy Solar System constraints, moving beyond case-by-case analyses toward a systematic classification framework.
item.dc:creator: Jie Li, Iftikhar Ahmad, Muhammad Mahtisham, Adnan Malik, Wenbin Lin, Fatemah Mofarreh

item.title: Black hole evaporation: From frontier physics to the classroom
item.description: arXiv:2611.31291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Half a century ago, Stephen Hawking discovered that black holes have a temperature, emit thermal radiation, and evaporate. Although Hawking temperature has been widely discussed in this journal, the evaporation process has received less attention. This work presents an accessible analysis of black hole evaporation, addressing the main questions raised by this phenomenon through intuitive ideas and heuristic calculations. It is shown that a problem situated at the frontier of physics can be reformulated in terms accessible for exploration in the classroom. In this sense, the article constitutes an educational resource that enables the integration of concepts from thermodynamics, relativity, and quantum mechanics within a meaningful learning context.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Pinochet

item.title: Curvature-Orbit Quantization of Gauge-Related Connections and a Radon--Nikodym Route to Lattice Yang--Mills Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.31309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a four-dimensional gauge construction in which two gauge-related non-abelian connections, $A=B^g$, interact only through the squared difference of their curvatures. Independent kinetic term is absent. The action is an ultralocal functional on a curvature orbit. Its Hessian is a pointwise positive-semidefinite operator whose kernel is the common stabilizer algebra of the curvature components, and its spectrum is given for every compact simple Lie group. At a finite regulator the model is an exact compact-group integral. Integrating out the orbit variable yields a positive, bounded Radon--Nikodym cocycle that relates the induced link measure to a lattice Yang--Mills measure, recasting the existence and mass-gap question as a uniform estimate on this cocycle.
item.dc:creator: Victor Atanasov

item.title: Scalaron initial conditions and regular-branch response in quadratic scalar-vector-tensor cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.31317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate the metric quadratic-curvature representation of a scalar-vector-tensor dark-energy background, keeping the nonzero temporal-vector solution used in the general-relativistic theory. We show that the additional curvature degree of freedom can influence on the choice of initial condition. We find that changing the initial curvature or its derivative alters the effective pattern of the phantom-divide crossing. We also analyze the rapid homogeneous curvature oscillation and obtain its leading frequency and damping in the presence of the temporal vector. As a result, we demonstrate that for the branch obtained by omitting the free scalaron mode, order reduction gives only a small normalized change in distance over the reference coupling interval used as the test of the consistency. Furthermore, we perform that the information diagnostic cannot be interpreted as an observational bound on the coupling term of the quadratic curvature.
item.dc:creator: G. G. N. Nashed, Kazuharu Bamba

item.title: Exact reconstruction of running vacuum cosmology in torsion and nonmetricity gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.31353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Running vacuum cosmology provides a dynamical description of vacuum energy while retaining the strict equation of state $w_{\rm DE}=-1$. However, whether its complete cosmological dynamics can emerge from a gravitational Lagrangian remains an important theoretical question. In this work, we investigate this possibility within torsion and nonmetricity gravity, considering minimally coupled, nonminimal matter-coupled, and trace-coupled theories. We first reconstruct analytically the running vacuum energy density in $f(T)$ and $f(Q)$ gravity, showing that energy density matching does not generally imply identical equations of state or expansion histories. We quantify these differences using Pantheon+, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 BAO data. However, considering trace-coupled $f(T,\mathcal{T})$ and $f(Q,\mathcal{T})$ gravity we extract explicit gravitational Lagrangians that exactly reproduce the complete running vacuum dynamics at the background level, namely both Friedmann equations, the strict vacuum equation of state, the matter-vacuum interaction, and the resulting expansion history. Furthermore, we identify regular solutions approaching a future de Sitter attractor, with positive matter and vacuum densities. Our results establish an explicit gravitational realization of running vacuum cosmology, extending beyond the mere matching of its effective vacuum energy density.
item.dc:creator: Fotios K. Anagnostopoulos, Spyros Basilakos, Eftychios E. Chalkiadakis, Stefanos Pigkas-Balanikas, Panagiotis G. Stavros, Emmanuel N. Saridakis

item.title: Physical Selection of Cartan Soft Breakings in a Broken $SU(3)$ Yang--Mills Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.31961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the broken-$SU(3)$ Yang--Mills model with soft quadratic breaking induced by the dimension-two operator $d^{abc}A_\mu^bA_\mu^c$, previously studied for a physical source aligned along the color-3 direction. We extend the construction to a generic Cartan-valued source and determine the corresponding quadratic propagators and their associated $i$-particle structure. We show that the diagonal $(3,8)$ sector always reorganizes into a conjugate pair of complex modes and therefore supports a physical one-loop composite channel with a K\"all\'en--Lehmann spectral representation. By contrast, the replica-like off-diagonal channel built from the $(4,5)$ and $(6,7)$ sectors survives as an admissible physical channel only on a special locus in the Cartan plane. In this sense, the original color-3 model is not merely a convenient example: it is dynamically singled out by the simultaneous survival of the neutral off-diagonal physical channel together with the diagonal one. The resulting picture provides a sharper understanding of the relation between soft color breaking, confinement-inspired propagators, and the construction of physically meaningful composite operators in confining gauge theories. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this distinguished soft-breaking structure can be dynamically generated via a BRST-invariant spontaneous symmetry breaking mechanism that preserves the strict algebraic renormalizability of the theory.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Amaral, V. E. R. Lemes
